# ClickTrail

ClickTrail is the open-source attribution handoff layer for developers and coding agents. It keeps observed acquisition context attached to conversion records inside the stack a team owns, including leads, sales, orders, and offline conversions.

## Canonical protocol

CAPTURE -> PERSIST -> CARRY -> ATTACH -> REPORT -> DEDUPE -> VERIFY

## Problem-oriented skills

- google-ads-offline-conversions: preserve GCLID, GBRAID, and WBRAID from ad click to CRM or Google Ads conversion.
- meta-capi-deduplication: match browser Pixel and server CAPI events with event_id.
- preserve-click-ids: survive redirects, SPA navigation, cookies, and privacy storage limits.
- cross-domain-attribution: transfer signed attribution context between domains.
- lead-to-sale-attribution: connect anonymous visits to leads and delayed sales.
- crm-revenue-attribution: connect CRM revenue to advertising identifiers.
- attribution-debugging: find where attribution was lost.
- conversion-reconciliation: compare CRM and destination conversion records.

Install: `npx skills add vizuh/clicktrail-skills`

## Grok Build

Grok Build can load the existing Claude-compatible ClickTrail plugin. The
problem-oriented `click-tracking-audit` skill routes requests such as “check my
click tracking,” lost GCLID/GBRAID/WBRAID/FBCLID, UTM persistence, offline
conversion tracking, GA4 versus Google Ads discrepancies, and CRM click-ID
handoffs. The plugin marketplace draft is in `grok/marketplace-entry.json`.
Local ClickTrail MCP remains a checked-out stdio server until its npm package is
published; local synthetic results do not prove provider delivery.

## Machine-completion workflow

The local MCP server exposes `inspect_project`, `detect_attribution_gaps`,
`plan_installation`, `simulate_ad_click`, `verify_capture`,
`verify_form_attachment`, `verify_crm_attachment`, `verify_conversion_delivery`,
and `attribution_health`. Synthetic passes do not prove live provider delivery.
